sources.title: GPT-5.6 Cyber — API model documentation
sources.evidence: Exact model ID and title; describes an alias for purpose-trained cybersecurity models requiring separate approval and provisioning. Lists 400,000-token context, 272,000 maximum input, 128,000 maximum output, text/image input, text output, reasoning tokens, function calling and Responses tools. Only the undated gpt-5.6-cyber identifier is listed as a snapshot.

sources.title: API changelog — August 7, 2026
sources.evidence: The August 7, 2026 feature entry names gpt-5.6-cyber and says Daybreak now offers separately approved access to purpose-trained models such as GPT-5.6 Cyber through Daybreak Red and the Responses API.

sources.title: Expanding Daybreak as the cyber defense window narrows
sources.evidence: August 10, 2026 announcement explicitly says GPT-5.6 Cyber is built on GPT-5.6 Sol and trained for cybersecurity, with access for approved defenders. Its benchmark footnote describes reasoning budgets. It says a separate Cyber system card will be published later; the announcement gives no model parameter counts or production architecture.

sources.title: File inputs
sources.evidence: Responses accepts PDF file inputs. For vision-capable models the API extracts both document text and page images. This applies through the exact Cyber page listing image input and Responses support; it does not imply native PDF tokens or a distinct production modality encoder.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: The agreement provides limited nonexclusive access to business services and APIs, while section 9.1 reserves OpenAI intellectual-property rights. Together with separately approved hosted model access, this supports a descriptive Proprietary classification, not an open-weight license.

sources.title: All models
sources.evidence: Lists GPT-5.6 Cyber as a hosted model; the separately labeled open-weight section names gpt-oss models instead. No Cyber weights or open-weight license are offered here.

sources.title: GPT-5.6 System Card
sources.evidence: The July 9 family card describes Sol, Terra and Luna. The complete text was checked for the exact Cyber model and structural/parameter disclosures; it does not identify this later Cyber variant or disclose its total or active parameters. Family members are not substituted for this model.

sources.title: GPT-6 Astra System Card — Table 21
sources.evidence: Later first-party Table 21 on printed page 110 has an exact gpt-5.6-Cyber with Daybreak Red comparison column. It reports defensive cybersecurity task completion rates, not parameter counts, active parameters or architectural structure.

sources.title: Prompt caching
sources.evidence: The current guide describes key/value intermediate states and distinct GPT-5.6-and-later cache behavior. The exact Cyber page lists prompt caching, but the guide does not explicitly identify Cyber as a Transformer or establish dense versus mixture-of-experts structure. KV caching alone is not used as architectural proof.

sources.title: How GPT-5.6 fuses frontier intelligence with frontier efficiency
sources.evidence: July 29 engineering article discusses inference improvements, sub-networks, and speculative draft-model architecture experiments. It gives no exact Cyber parameter counts or production architecture. Draft-model design and generic sub-network language are not treated as Transformer or MoE disclosures for Cyber, even though the Cyber announcement names Sol as its base.

sources.title: Deprecations
sources.evidence: The complete current deprecation document was checked for the exact gpt-5.6-cyber identifier; no exact-model retirement entry was found. This does not test live endpoint operation.

sources.title: Attempted GPT-5.6 Cyber system-card PDF location
sources.evidence: The attempted conventional deployment-safety PDF URL returned HTTP 404. This is a failed lookup, not evidence that no Cyber card exists elsewhere.

name.note: Exact display name in the official model documentation and announcement.

family.note: The exact model identifier is gpt-5.6-cyber; the announcement explicitly identifies GPT-5.6 Sol as its base. Replace the overly broad gpt family.

release_date.note: Retain August 7: the dated API changelog explicitly offers Cyber through separately approved Daybreak Red. August 10 is the later public announcement. Earlier customer previews mentioned without dates do not establish an earlier public release.

open_weights.note: Hosted, separately approved Daybreak access; the official catalog distinguishes its open-weight models and does not offer Cyber weights.

license.note: Descriptive classification of the hosted service under OpenAI terms; no Cyber open-weight distribution license is documented.

parameters_b.note: No total parameter count is disclosed in the checked exact-model announcement, API page or later Astra comparison. Searches of first-party technical, training and interpretability material found no exact Cyber count. Do not transfer Sol or draft-model scale.

active_parameters_b.note: No active parameter count is given for this exact model in the checked sources. No dense or MoE assumption is made, and active parameters are not equated to an unknown total.

architecture.note: Exact production structure remains unverified. The announcement explicitly establishes derivation from Sol, but checked first-party sources do not establish Sol or Cyber topology. Current KV caching, generic sub-networks and speculative draft-model experiments are insufficient. Older pre-GPT-5.6 caching descriptions are not used. A separate Cyber card was not located; the attempted PDF URL returned 404.

context_window.note: Current exact-model documentation states 400,000 total context, maximum input 272,000 and maximum output 128,000. A generic pricing line for longer prompts is not taken as evidence of a larger input limit. Documented specification, not a live endpoint test.

modalities.note: Native documented input is text/image and output is text. Add PDF as a supported Responses input format: the API converts PDFs into extracted text and page images for this explicitly vision-capable model. Hosted image-generation tools do not imply native image output; no audio/video input is documented.

reasoning.note: Exact model page explicitly supports reasoning tokens; the announcement discusses Cyber reasoning budgets. No unsupported reasoning-effort enum is inferred.

tool_call.note: Exact model page explicitly lists function_calling and Responses tools including web/file search, code interpreter, hosted shell, apply_patch, skills, computer use, MCP and tool search. Chat Completions is not supported.

description.value: Cybersecurity model for authorized vulnerability research and security testing
description.note: Retain the factual description; it matches the documented authorized defensive scope without comparative marketing claims. Access restrictions are recorded in notes.

patch.notes: Released through separately approved Daybreak Red access on August 7, 2026; the announcement followed on August 10. GPT-5.6 Cyber is an undated alias for purpose-trained cybersecurity models, built on GPT-5.6 Sol, and requires separate approval and provisioning. Current documentation lists 400,000 total context, 272,000 maximum input and 128,000 maximum output, with reasoning tokens, function calling and Responses tools; Chat Completions is unsupported. PDF is an API input format converted to extracted text and page images, not evidence of a native PDF encoder. Total and active parameter counts are undisclosed in the checked primary sources; production architecture remains unverified. The original family card does not cover the exact Cyber variant, and the later Astra card compares Cyber performance without structural specifications. A separate Cyber card was not located; the attempted deployment-safety PDF URL returned 404. Only the undated model alias is listed, no exact deprecation was found in the current deprecation document, and endpoint operation was not tested.

summary: Confirm August 7 restricted public API release and current 400K context, reasoning, tool calling and authorized-security description. Narrow family to gpt-5.6, classify the hosted service as Proprietary, add supported PDF input format and replace catalog-only provenance with primary sources. Total/active parameter counts remain undisclosed; architecture remains unverified after exact-model and later comparison checks. No sibling, speculative draft-model or old caching architecture is transferred.
